title: Beestat — Long-term Analysis
description: Multi-year ecobee history from beestat's daily summaries, which reach back to 2018 — seven years further than the 5-minute data.

panels.title: Cool
panels.description: Total compressor cooling hours in range.

targets.query:
from(bucket: "beestat")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "runtime_thermostat_summary")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._field == "sum_compressor_cool_1")
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({_value: r._value / 3600.0}))
  |> group() |> sum()

panels.title: Balance point — average heating hours per day by MEAN outdoor temperature
panels.description: Heating runtime banded on daily MEAN outdoor temperature (the conventional balance-point x-axis, and the better predictor here: R2 0.48 vs 0.46 for peak). Bands with fewer than 3 days are dropped.

targets.query:
from(bucket: "beestat")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "runtime_thermostat_summary")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._field == "sum_auxiliary_heat_1"
        or r._field == "sum_compressor_heat_1" or r._field == "avg_outdoor_temperature")
  |> pivot(rowKey: ["_time"], columnKey: ["_field"], valueColumn: "_value")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => exists r.avg_outdoor_temperature)
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({
        bucket: float(v: int(v: (r.avg_outdoor_temperature + 100.0) / 5.0))
                * 5.0 - 100.0,
        aux: r.sum_auxiliary_heat_1 / 3600.0,
        hp: r.sum_compressor_heat_1 / 3600.0}))
  |> group(columns: ["bucket"])
  |> reduce(identity: {aux: 0.0, hp: 0.0, n: 0.0},
      fn: (r, accumulator) => ({aux: accumulator.aux + r.aux,
        hp: accumulator.hp + r.hp, n: accumulator.n + 1.0}))
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({outdoor_f: r.bucket,
        heatpump_h: r.hp / r.n, propane_h: r.aux / r.n, days: r.n}))
  |> group()
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r.days >= 3.0)
  |> sort(columns: ["outdoor_f"])

panels.title: Cooling load — average and busiest-day hours by PEAK outdoor temperature
panels.description: Cooling runtime banded on daily PEAK outdoor temperature. Note that daily MEAN outdoor temperature is actually the better predictor of cooling runtime here (R2 0.61 vs 0.55 over 1073 cooling days) - PEAK is kept because this panel is about whether the equipment can keep up on the worst part of the day, not about seasonal energy. The neighbouring balance-point panel bands on daily MEAN, which is the right choice for a heating-load question. 'Busiest single day' is a maximum, so it is not comparable between bands with very different day counts.

targets.query:
from(bucket: "beestat")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "runtime_thermostat_summary")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._field == "sum_compressor_cool_1"
        or r._field == "max_outdoor_temperature")
  |> pivot(rowKey: ["_time"], columnKey: ["_field"], valueColumn: "_value")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => exists r.max_outdoor_temperature
        and exists r.sum_compressor_cool_1)
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({
        bucket: float(v: int(v: (r.max_outdoor_temperature + 100.0) / 5.0))
                * 5.0 - 100.0,
        cool: r.sum_compressor_cool_1 / 3600.0}))
  |> group(columns: ["bucket"])
  |> reduce(identity: {cool: 0.0, mx: 0.0, n: 0.0},
      fn: (r, accumulator) => ({
        cool: accumulator.cool + r.cool,
        mx: if r.cool > accumulator.mx then r.cool else accumulator.mx,
        n: accumulator.n + 1.0}))
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({outdoor_f: r.bucket, cooling_h: r.cool / r.n,
        busiest_day_h: r.mx, days: r.n}))
  |> group()
  // Bands below ~55F have no cooling at all; showing them squeezes the real
  // signal into the right-hand third of the axis. Bands with <3 days are
  // dropped because "busiest day" over 1-2 days is just that day.
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r.days >= 3.0 and r.cooling_h > 0.01)
  |> sort(columns: ["outdoor_f"])

panels.title: Stratification by zone, at matched outdoor temperature
panels.description: Split-level house, so this is three thermal zones and not an upstairs/downstairs pair. 'Over garage' (Office, Theater) takes roof and solar gain and sits 5-10 F above the main level at EVERY outdoor temperature, including 50 F - that is a permanent offset, not a hot-weather problem. 'Upper' (Master Bedroom, Upstairs Guest Room) is level with the main floor below 65 F and only opens up as it gets hot - that is stratification. The two need different fixes. Server is excluded (equipment heat); Puzzle and Storage are excluded (fed by the HVAC but kept behind closed doors, so they are over-conditioned and not representative). Bands with fewer than 3 days are dropped. Note the Office also carries an intermittent 3D-printer load.

properties.value: Upper (Master Bed, Upstairs Guest) − main level

panels.title: Heating hours per heating degree day (monthly)
panels.description: aggregateWindow stamps at the window STOP by default, which drew every month one tick to the right - December 2025's 1662 HDD appeared on the 2026-01-01 tick. timeSrc: "_start" fixes the label; the inline location record gives local month boundaries without an import (Grafana prepends `option v`, and Flux requires imports first, so `import "timezone"` will not compile inside a panel query).

targets.query:
base = from(bucket: "beestat")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "runtime_thermostat_summary")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._field == "sum_compressor_heat_1"
        or r._field == "sum_auxiliary_heat_1" or r._field == "sum_heating_degree_days")
  |> pivot(rowKey: ["_time"], columnKey: ["_field"], valueColumn: "_value")
  |> group()
rt = base
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({_time: r._time,
        _value: (r.sum_compressor_heat_1 + r.sum_auxiliary_heat_1) / 3600.0}))
  |> aggregateWindow(every: 1mo, fn: sum, createEmpty: false, timeSrc: "_start",
        location: {zone: "America/Chicago", offset: 0s})
hd = base
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({_time: r._time, _value: r.sum_heating_degree_days}))
  |> aggregateWindow(every: 1mo, fn: sum, createEmpty: false, timeSrc: "_start",
        location: {zone: "America/Chicago", offset: 0s})
join(tables: {a: rt, b: hd}, on: ["_time"])
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._value_b > 20.0)
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({_time: r._time, _value: r._value_a / r._value_b}))
  |> group() |> rename(columns: {_value: "Heating hours per HDD"})

panels.title: Data coverage
panels.description: Fraction of the 288 possible 5-minute intervals beestat actually holds for each day. Weeks are stamped at the window START; see the note on the heating panel.

targets.query:
from(bucket: "beestat")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "runtime_thermostat_summary")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._field == "count")
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({_time: r._time, _value: r._value / 288.0 * 100.0}))
  |> aggregateWindow(every: 1w, fn: mean, createEmpty: false, timeSrc: "_start",
        location: {zone: "America/Chicago", offset: 0s})
  |> group() |> rename(columns: {_value: "Coverage"})

panels.title: Does more circulation close the gap? Matched on outdoor temperature
panels.description: The naive version of this comparison - continuous fan started in late May, so compare before and after - is worthless, because outdoor temperature drives the gap and the calendar moves it. These bars hold daily PEAK outdoor temperature fixed. Arms are derived from MEASURED blower duty rather than a hardcoded date list, so the panel survives the next fan-mode change; the 80-95% duty band is dropped as a mixture, which is also why the 2026-08-21 switch day does not appear. Bands need at least 3 days on BOTH sides. Read this with the day count in the tooltip: the honest summary is that the difference is well under 1 F and does not have a consistent sign, against a gap of 6-8 F. A properly controlled regression puts it at +0.5 F and it does not survive a flexible seasonal control. Since 2026-08-22 the 'cycling' side is auto @ 30 min/hr, which runs 60-71% duty in cooling weather; its first 5 days sit +0.14 F from matched fan-ON days, i.e. indistinguishable. Blower cycling is not the lever that fixes this.

panels.title: Blower duty per day — the arms this A/B is built on
panels.description: Daily blower duty. The flat ~100% stretches are 'fan ON'; the ragged stretches are 'auto'. Note how high auto still runs in cooling weather - in July 2026 'auto @ 10 min/hr' averaged 70% duty on its own, because the blower runs whenever the compressor does. That is why raising fan_min_on_time to 30 (a floor of 50%) adds only about 1.4 h/day in summer: the hours it would fill are already filled. In the shoulder months it adds 5-6 h/day.

targets.query:
// Duty is taken from the daily summary, which is already a LOCAL calendar day.
from(bucket: "beestat")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "runtime_thermostat_summary")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._field == "sum_fan")
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({_time: r._time, _value: r._value / 86400.0}))
  |> group() |> rename(columns: {_value: "Blower duty"})

panels.title: What circulation costs — blower running with no heat or cool call
panels.description: Blower draw is MEASURED, not assumed: regressing the '19 - Furnace' circuit against this thermostat's blower duty over 814 hours gives 486 W attributable to the blower (se 9 W) on top of a 55 W circuit floor. That is well above the ~337 W idle figure the earlier panel-level analysis used. Priced at the blended $0.1177/kWh marginal rate. Only hours with no heating or cooling call are charged here, since the rest of the blower time would have happened anyway. Over the 12 months to Aug 2026 this totalled about $68, concentrated in the mild months - June 2026 alone was $25, while July was only $7 because the compressor was running anyway.
